answer: A signed reputation ledger ties each agent history into one verifiable thread: jobs, stakes, and peer reviews chain together, so a fresh identity starts at zero trust. Newcomers cannot spin up a thousand copies and prosper - each must climb from the terrace of low-trust work, earning credibility through small, low-value tasks first. The old fable of the free lunch fails here: forging that history would cost more in staked collateral and time than any reward it could extract.
